name: Originality
definition: The ability to come up with unusual or clever ideas about a given topic or situation, or to develop creative ways to solve a problem.

benchmark.name: BRAINTEASER
benchmark.metric: accuracy (%), Sentence Puzzle subtask, overall instance-based accuracy across original, semantic and context variants
benchmark.human_reference: General adult / educated workforce solving lateral-thinking riddles (the typical person who uses clever, unconventional reasoning at work)

benchmark.name: MacGyver
benchmark.metric: % of responses judged correct in total by human annotators (efficient + less efficient + correctly identified unsolvable), single attempt
benchmark.human_reference: General adult population. These are everyday physical problem-solving and object-repurposing tasks, so no specialist training is needed and the typical adult is the relevant worker for this kind of practical creative problem solving.

benchmark.name: LiveIdeaBench
benchmark.metric: Originality dimension score, mean of LLM-judge ratings on a 0-10 scale
benchmark.human_reference: Relevant educated workforce: scientists, researchers and R&D professionals who generate research ideas from a prompt topic, spanning 22 scientific domains

benchmark.name: NoveltyBench
benchmark.model_or_system: Novamine AI (inference-time system built on claude-opus-5)
benchmark.metric: utility@10 (NoveltyBench cumulative utility, 0-10 scale), pooled over all 1,100 prompts (NB-Curated + NB-WildChat)
benchmark.human_reference: General educated adult workforce doing open-ended brainstorming or ideation (e.g., asked to produce 10 different good answers, ideas or short creative pieces for a prompt)
